questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Your skin is constantly making new cells and shedding old ones, so it is always renewing itself.

questions.question: Roughly how many bones are there in an adult human body?
questions.explanation: Babies are born with around 300 bones, and many of them join together as they grow.

questions.question: Where in your body is the smallest bone?
questions.explanation: The stirrup bone, deep inside your ear, is about the size of a grain of rice.

questions.question: Which gas does your body need from the air you breathe in?
questions.explanation: Your lungs pass oxygen into your blood, which carries it to every part of your body.

questions.question: Which part of your blood helps a cut stop bleeding?
questions.explanation: Platelets rush to a cut and clump together to plug the gap, which is how a scab begins.

questions.question: How many sets of teeth do people grow in their lives?
questions.explanation: Your 20 milk teeth are replaced by up to 32 adult teeth.

questions.question: What is the hardest thing in the human body?
questions.explanation: Enamel, the shiny outer layer of your teeth, is even harder than bone.

questions.question: About how many times a minute does a resting adult's heart beat?
questions.explanation: That adds up to around 100,000 heartbeats every single day.

questions.question: Which part of your eye makes your pupil smaller in bright light?
questions.explanation: Your iris is the coloured part of your eye, and it makes the pupil shrink in bright light and grow in the dark.

questions.question: Which sense helps you taste your food more than any other?
questions.explanation: That is why food tastes of very little when you have a blocked nose.

questions.question: What is the name of your thigh bone, the longest bone in your body?
questions.explanation: Your femur is about a quarter as long as you are tall.

questions.question: What does your stomach use to help break down food?
questions.explanation: Your stomach makes a strong acid, and a layer of slimy mucus stops it from digesting itself.

questions.question: Which bones make a cage that protects your heart and lungs?
questions.explanation: Most people have 12 pairs of ribs.

questions.question: When you get goosebumps, what are tiny muscles in your skin doing?
questions.explanation: Furry animals do it to trap warm air or look bigger; for us it is a leftover from our hairier ancestors.

questions.question: Which muscle suddenly tightening causes a hiccup?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm jerks, and the 'hic' is the sound of your vocal cords snapping shut.

questions.question: What is the medical name for the voice box?
questions.explanation: The bump at the front of the throat called the Adam's apple is part of the larynx.

questions.question: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.explanation: Insulin, made in the pancreas, lets the body's cells take in sugar from the blood.

questions.question: Which vitamin does your skin make when it is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium, which keeps bones and teeth strong.

questions.question: What is the medical name for the kneecap?
questions.explanation: The patella sits inside a tendon in front of the knee joint, protecting it.

questions.question: Who developed the first vaccine, against smallpox, in 1796?
questions.explanation: Jenner noticed that milkmaids who caught cowpox seemed safe from smallpox, and the word vaccine comes from the Latin for cow.

questions.question: What is the medical name for the collarbone?
questions.explanation: The clavicle is one of the most commonly broken bones, often in a fall onto an outstretched arm.

questions.question: People with which blood group are known as universal donors of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: O negative red cells can be given to almost anyone, which is why hospitals use them in emergencies.

questions.question: Which is the heaviest organ inside the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver weighs about 1.5 kg and can grow back after part of it is removed.

questions.question: What is the name of the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin contains iron, which is what gives blood its red colour.

questions.question: Roughly how much of an adult's body weight is water?
questions.explanation: Even your bones are made partly of water.

questions.question: Which English doctor first described how blood circulates round the body, in 1628?
questions.explanation: Harvey showed that the heart pumps the same blood round and round the body in a loop.

questions.question: Roughly how long is the small intestine in an adult?
questions.explanation: Coiled up inside you, the small intestine is far longer than you are tall.

questions.question: Which part of the brain mainly controls balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: Cerebellum means 'little brain', and it sits at the back of the head, under the main part of the brain.

questions.question: Which part of the body contains the most bones?
questions.explanation: Your two hands contain 54 bones between them, more than a quarter of all the bones in your body.

questions.question: Which glands produce tears?
questions.explanation: The lacrimal glands sit above the outer corner of each eye and keep it moist with every blink.
